key_insight: The paper turns DFT fallback into a risk-controlled selection problem, using conformal risk control to decide which configurations need expensive DFT labels and which can safely keep MLIP predictions.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster high-throughput materials screening by reducing DFT calls while enforcing a user-specified bound on tolerated MLIP error.
method: Build a structure-only geometric descriptor from atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates.
Train a lightweight predictor to estimate MLIP-DFT disagreement in energy, average force, and maximum force.
Calibrate the predicted disagreement with conformal risk control to set a DFT-selection threshold with guaranteed residual-error control.
evidence_signal: Across eight dataset-MLIP pairs, the method routed 7% to 14% fewer configurations to DFT at α=0.3 than committee baselines while maintaining the same risk guarantee.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the predictor generalizes across dataset shifts; gains shrink when the DFT labels and MLIP training data use the same functional and basis set.
paper_title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
